Featured Maps

Thematic Cartography

Allocation of Water Resources — Africa

A continental choropleth of baseline water stress, classified by country and overlaid with major watershed boundaries. Source data reconciled from the WRI Aqueduct 4.0 water-risk framework and HydroSHEDS basins, projected in Africa Albers Equal Area Conic for honest area comparison.

ArcGIS ProWRI AqueductHydroSHEDSEqual-Area Projection
Reference & Statistical Mapping

North Korea — Population Density

Modeled population density draped over a shaded-relief base to reveal how terrain shapes settlement. Built from WorldPop 2020 estimates and a Copernicus digital elevation model, with a custom seven-class, data-driven break scheme tuned to the distribution’s extreme skew.

ArcGIS ProWorldPopCopernicus DEMHillshade
3D Data Visualization

Residential CO₂ Emissions — Shanghai

A three-dimensional treatment of gridded residential carbon emissions, where each cell is extruded by its annual output to turn a flat raster into a skyline of consumption. Gridded EDGAR emissions data processed in ArcGIS Pro and rendered in Blender.

ArcGIS ProBlenderEDGARRaster → Vector
Terrain & Relief

Chechnya & the North Caucasus

A shaded-relief terrain map emphasizing the dramatic topography of the Greater Caucasus, with hypsometric tinting, vertical exaggeration, and vector overlays for borders, rivers, and settlements. Built from a Copernicus DEM in an ArcGIS Pro 3D scene with a locator inset.

ArcGIS Pro 3DCopernicus DEMHypsometric TintVector Overlay
Terrain & Relief

Mount Greylock — Historic Sheet in Relief

A three-dimensional relief treatment of the 1898 U.S. Geological Survey Greylock sheet (Massachusetts–Vermont). The original historic quadrangle is draped over elevation data so the Berkshires rise in true relief, while the antique linework, neatline, and typography are preserved intact.

BlenderUSGS Historic TopoDEM3D Relief

About

I’m a GIS and cartographic professional based in the Greater Boston area, currently a Maps & Records Coordinator at National Grid. My background sits at the intersection of environmental science, spatial analysis, and visual communication — I hold a B.A. in Earth & Environmental Science (GIS & Remote Sensing) from Boston University and am pursuing an M.S. in Applied Data Analytics.

My work spans the full cartographic pipeline: collecting and integrating geographic data, performing QA/QC and data conversion, designing honest and legible thematic maps, and building both static products and interactive web applications. I care about the craft — projection choices, classification, typography, and data integrity — and about making spatial information genuinely useful to the people who rely on it.
